name: PLLA / Sculptra perioral

card.summary: A collagen-stimulating injectable used around the mouth; perioral evidence in the sources reviewed is one ongoing trial.
card.note: Clinician-administered; no perioral trial results available in sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
PLLA is the active ingredient in Sculptra, an injectable that stimulates the skin to make collagen. People use it around the mouth to soften wrinkles and restore support gradually.

A phase 4 trial of topical PLLA with microneedling for perioral wrinkles is recruiting; no results were found.
quick.mechanism: The material triggers a foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release signals such as TGF-beta, prompting fibroblasts to produce collagen. It degrades over about six months to two years into lactic acid.
quick.risks: Nodules are a recognised concern with injectable collagen stimulators generally, though the sources reviewed did not detail rates. It is a clinician-administered product; rules vary by country.

lead: PLLA / Sculptra perioral refers to injecting poly-L-lactic acid (the active ingredient in Sculptra) around the mouth to soften lines and restore the support that gives the lower face a fuller, smoother look. It is a collagen stimulator: instead of adding instant volume the way a hyaluronic acid filler does, it prompts the skin to build collagen over weeks to months, so the lines, hollowing and loss of firmness around the lips and chin improve gradually [1][2][3].

PLLA is a synthetic, biocompatible, biodegradable polymer. A 2018 review describes how the size and chemistry of its microparticles produce a subclinical inflammatory response that stimulates collagen deposition in the extracellular matrix, restoring volume in a controlled way that lasts [3]. Wikipedia describes a foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release signalling molecules such as TGF-beta that prompt fibroblasts to make collagen [1]. Sculptra has been approved for facial aesthetic use since 1999 in Europe and since 2009 in the USA [4].

Systematic reviews of PLLA in the face report improvements in skin quality, wrinkles and volume with effects lasting up to about 25 months [2][5]. Trials focused on the perioral area specifically are limited to one registered study of topical PLLA combined with microneedling [6]. On looksmax.org a user who looks gaunt when losing weight has asked about Sculptra as a way to restore facial fullness [7].

chain: PLLA microparticles injected into the target area
Local response stimulates fibroblasts to produce collagen
Gradual restoration of volume, firmness and smoother lines over months
angle.text: Clinicians use PLLA to rebuild support and soften lines around the mouth and lower face through gradual collagen production. People seeking it describe wanting a less hollow, less aged lower face and a firmer, smoother perioral area.

infobox: Injection; topical with microneedling under study [6]
Effects sustained up to about 25 months in reviews [2][5]
About 6 months to 2 years for PLA implants (reference estimate) [1]

paras: Sculptra is used as an injectable to add facial volume and improve skin quality [1][2]. In perioral treatment clinicians use it to address fine lines and loss of support around the mouth through gradual collagen production, rather than to add immediate lip volume. Because collagen builds over time, results appear progressively rather than on the day of treatment [3].

Reviews describe PLLA being combined with other approaches, such as botulinum toxin, dermal fillers and energy-based devices, though a 2025 systematic review described studies of such combinations as sparse and varied in method [8]. A 2024 randomised trial reported that microneedling radiofrequency enhanced PLLA penetration and improved facial skin laxity [9].
The same material is used for HIV-associated facial lipodystrophy [1], and an international consensus has examined it for body areas such as neck, knees, abdomen, hands, upper arms and cellulite [4].

PLLA microparticles provoke a mild foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release mediators including TGF-beta that signal fibroblasts to produce collagen [1][3]. A 2025 gene-expression study compared PLLA with calcium hydroxylapatite and reported that PLLA triggered regeneration-related gene activity while calcium hydroxylapatite was associated with inflammation-related activity [10].

Polylactic acid implants break down over roughly six months to two years into lactic acid, which the reference article describes as innocuous [1]. A 2024 histology study examined how long the biostimulatory activity of injectable PLLA lasts [11].

A 2024 systematic review of eleven randomised trials reported that adverse events were mild to moderate and mainly bruising, haematoma, tenderness, nodules and oedema [5]. A 2026 systematic review found mild effects such as pain and swelling at the injection site to be the most frequent [2]. Nodules are a recognised concern with injectable collagen stimulators and are discussed in clinical reviews of the technique [5].

A 2024 systematic review in Polymers included eleven randomised trials of PLLA for facial ageing or lipoatrophy; four reported increased dermal thickness and improved lipoatrophy and aesthetic scores sustained for at least 25 months, and some found PLLA superior to injectable human collagen or to a comparison gel [5]. A 2026 systematic review of fourteen studies found both PLLA and calcium hydroxyapatite improved skin elasticity, wrinkles and facial volume, with PLLA effects lasting up to 25 months [2]. Randomised trials have examined Sculptra for cheek wrinkles against no treatment [12] and compared a newer PLLA filler with Sculptra for nasolabial folds [13].

For the perioral area itself, the registered phase 4 trial NCT07225348 (26 participants, started November 2025) tests topical PLLA with a microneedling device for perioral wrinkles; no results were available at last listing [6].

timeline.event: Sculptra approved for facial aesthetic use in Europe.[4]
Sculptra approved for facial aesthetic use in the USA.[4]
Phase 4 trial of topical PLLA with microneedling for perioral wrinkles begins recruiting.[6]

lore.intro: Sculptra is discussed on looksmax.org mainly as an option for facial hollowing, for example after weight loss [7].

claims.claim: Sculptra can fix a gaunt face after weight loss
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user who looks gaunt when losing weight asked for opinions on Sculptra and said they were planning treatment within weeks, reflecting the view that it can restore lost facial fullness [7].
claims.experts: Systematic reviews report increased facial volume, dermal thickness and improved lipoatrophy scores after PLLA treatment, sustained up to about 25 months [2][5].
